question_text: A 55-year-old male presents to his primary care physician with right upper quadrant pain that has progressed over the last three months with unexplained weakness and joint pains that have been "out of the ordinary" over the last year. On history, you note the patient lives a sedentary lifestyle, rarely leaves the house, has controlled diabetes diagnosed 15 years ago, and has documented cardiomyopathy. On physical exam the man appears non-toxic, sclera are icteric, cornea appear normal, generalized pain is elicited on palpation of the right upper quadrant, and skin appears quite bronzed on his extremities. What is this patient most at risk for ten to fifteen years later due to his underlying condition?
